chunk.chapter_title: 55. Shabala creates an army which annihilates Vishwamitra's force
chunk.text:

Shabala, who was skilled in argument, listened to the words 
of Shri Vasishtha and said : " 0 Holy Sage, the power of a 
warrior is as nought a>mpared to that of a holy sage. 
0 Illustrious Lord, the strength of a sage is divine and based 
on the exercise of spiritual practices and discipline, it is therefore 
limitless ; thou art, 0 Lord, immeasurably stronger than a 
kshatriya. The power of that mighty king Vishwamitra, is 
great, but he cannot equal thy strength and splendour. 0 Lord, 
through thy strength and energy suffer me to destroy the power 
and pride of this wicked wretch." 
Shri Vasishtha answered : " Be it so I Create an army by 
thy spiritual energy, that will destroy the forces of the king." 
Lowing loudly, Sbabsla, in obedience to the sage, instantly

the army of Vishwamitra while he was looking on.

Then the great Vishwamitra, with the aid of yogic weapons,

Deprived of his glory, he resembled a waveless ocean or a snake

brief.summary_1line: Shabala magically creates armies that destroy Vishwamitra’s forces; his sons die, and the humiliated king turns to severe penance and seeks divine weapons from Shiva.

image_candidates.scene_text: The sacred cow Shabala bellows as armed warriors burst forth from her body while the battlefield fills with soldiers before the stunned army of Vishwamitra.
Vasishta calmly utters a single 'H'm' as the charging hundred sons of Vishwamitra are instantly burned to ashes before him.
A devastated Vishwamitra stands amid the ruins of his annihilated army, his chariot still and his face filled with shame beneath a darkened sky.

deep.rich_summary: Vasishtha’s divine cow Shabala defends her master against King Vishwamitra. Declaring that the spiritual power of a sage surpasses the might of a warrior, she asks permission to destroy the king’s pride. At Vasishtha’s command she miraculously generates armies—foreign soldiers and strange golden‑skinned warriors—who overwhelm Vishwamitra’s forces. Even when Vishwamitra counters with powerful weapons, Shabala produces more warriors from her own body, annihilating the king’s elephants, chariots, and troops. Vishwamitra’s hundred sons attack Vasishtha but are instantly burned to ashes when the sage utters a single sacred sound. Humiliated and stripped of glory, Vishwamitra abandons his kingdom and turns to severe asceticism. Winning the favor of Shiva, he gains divine knowledge and celestial weapons, setting the stage for a renewed confrontation with Vasishtha and marking the beginning of his transformation from king to spiritual seeker.

highlight_spans.why: Shabala declares the supremacy of a sage’s spiritual power over a warrior’s might, establishing the chapter’s core theme.
Shabala miraculously produces soldiers who begin destroying Vishwamitra’s army—one of the earliest displays of her supernatural power.
The strange golden-skinned warriors (Shakas) appear in vast numbers and consume the army like fire, escalating the battle into a mythic spectacle.
Warriors are born from Shabala’s body—feet, udders, hair, and thighs—showing the divine cow as a living source of limitless armies.
Vasishtha destroys Vishwamitra’s hundred sons with a single utterance, a dramatic moment demonstrating the overwhelming force of spiritual austerity.

top_scenes.scene_text: The divine cow Shabala stands beside sage Vasishtha as waves of warriors miraculously emerge from her body and charge across the battlefield.
Golden-skinned Shaka warriors in yellow armor surge across the earth like fire, overwhelming Vishwamitra’s chariots, elephants, and soldiers.
Sage Vasishtha calmly utters a single sacred sound while the hundred armed sons of Vishwamitra are instantly reduced to ashes before him.
